liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let It Grow** (4 reviews): The long jam in the second half goes somewhere dark and wild, a place the band hadn't reached before; Reviewer votes this the best version ever played [21][24][25][27]
- **Help on the Way** (2 reviews): Help on the Way, Slipknot and Franklin's Tower sequence rated among the best versions ever played; Help on the Way into Slipknot! and Franklin's Tower is among the best versions the reviewer has heard [25][27]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): By this song, Phil's bass was booming off the metal grandstand roof [23]
- **Might as Well** (1 review): A spinning circle of over 300 people began mid-song, energizing the band into setbreak and a strong second set [30]
- **Truckin'** (1 other source): A 16-second patch from the Nakamichi 700 source covers the noodle leading into Truckin' [10]
- **Wang Dang Doodle** (1 review): Stretched extra long because Bobby's mic broke; Jerry grew frustrated but then found the riff [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-09-11.125609.mtx.dusborne.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 184 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1983-09-11.fob.nak300.unknown.watson.100454.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 183 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Crisp and clean, with no cuts at cassette flips, suggesting it was mastered on PCM [4]
- **gd1983-09-11.152635.mtx.seamons.ht129.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: Clicks and static were cleaned up throughout; some sound-system static remains in an otherwise great-sounding soundboard [6]
- **gd83-09-11.sbd.dankseed.4995.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 172 min; rated 3.64/5 by 11 [7]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is excellent and a nice upgrade over the widely circulated high-quality audience recording; Mix is bass heavy, with the bass washed out or oversaturated, like a decent multigeneration cassette soundboard; Soundboard sound drops in and out frequently, making the quality poor [24][26][28]
- **gd1983-09-11.151510.fob.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 168 min [10]
- **gd83-09-11.sennheiser.4874.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 133 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [17]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is outstanding early digital, with well-placed mics and good dynamics; Phil's bass is solid but a bit lacking in air [22]

## Around the show

- On the morning of the second show, dozens of balloons lifted off for a race to Albuquerque [23]
- During set two tuning, a fan can be heard requesting The Wheel [4]
- Second set has rare standout moments scattered among otherwise ordinary material heard on countless tapes [21]
- Considered one of the year's best shows, with a second set hard to top [24]
- Not a top show of 1983; Sept. 2, 1983 is far better, and the second set beats an uninspired first [28]
- Very good for 1983 but not among the year's best [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-09-11.125609.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by dusborne; source: 2 Source Matrix Matrix by dusborne; Soundboard (shinid:4995) SBD>Master Cassette>1 Reel>DAT>DAT>WAV>Soundforge 4.0>CDWAV 1.53>MKW 0.97b>SHN DAT>WAV via Sony… [1]. Also: Matrix of Dankseed's soundboard with an audience DAT from Keith Litzenberger, transferred by Mike Watson [1]
- **gd1983-09-11.fob.nak300.unknown.watson.100454.flac16**: transferred by M. Watson; source: (FOB) Nakamichi CM300->PCM [4]. Also: Front-of-board Nakamichi 300 audience tape from Keith Litzenberger's DAT collection, transferred by Mike Watson; taper sat between Tony Suraci's position and this one [4]
- **gd1983-09-11.152635.mtx.seamons.ht129.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut > Soundtrack Pro > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) [6]. Also: Soundboard matrix uses audience source only for the first 2:53 of Alabama Getaway [6]
- **gd83-09-11.sbd.dankseed.4995.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Master Cassette>1 Reel> DAT> DAT> WAV> Soundforge 4.0> CDWAV 1.53> MKW 0.97b> SHN; source: SBD> Master Cassette [7]. Also: Soundboard fills its cuts with audience splices and is far better than an older cassette soundboard the reviewer had [25]
- **gd1983-09-11.151510.fob.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Robert Bryant's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; unknown mics > Sony D6 [10]
- **gd83-09-11.sennheiser.4874.sbeok.shnf**: source: Jeff Silberman's Master Audience PCM; Sennheiser 441 mics > Technics SV100 PCM > DAT > CDR> EAC> SHN; CD Remastering, EAC'ed / SHN'ed by Scott Clugston; to… [17]. Also: Complete soundboard in circulation is repaired with audience splices during a few dropouts; Jonathan Aizen is credited for its arrival [27]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Doug Collette: [Grateful Dead: Dave's Picks Volume 52 - The Downs At Santa Fe, Santa Fe, NM 9/11/83 (ALBUM REVIEW) - Glide Magazine](https://glidemagazine.com/308174/grateful-dead-daves-picks-volume-52-the-downs-at-santa-fe-santa-fe-nm-9-11-83-album-review/) [38]
- Fan art by www.bonhams.com: [Bonhams : Dennis Larkins: Grateful Dead at the Downs, Santa Fe, 10th-11th September 1983,](https://www.bonhams.com/auction/17108/lot/6307/dennis-larkins-grateful-dead-at-the-downs-santa-fe-10th-11th-september-1983/) [39]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Dave's Picks Vol. 52: The Downs at Santa Fe, Santa Fe, NM (9/11/83)](https://store.dead.net/products/daves-picks-vol-52-the-downs-at-santa-fe-santa-fe-nm-9-11-83?variant=42469430067242) [40]
- Poster by Zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead concert poster - Downs at Santa Fe, New Mexico, 9-10 and 9-11-83](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2196327887/) [41]
- Poster by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2196327887/) [42]

claims.text: The long jam in the second half goes somewhere dark and wild, a place the band hadn't reached before
Second set has rare standout moments scattered among otherwise ordinary material heard on countless tapes
Audience recording is outstanding early digital, with well-placed mics and good dynamics; Phil's bass is solid but a bit lacking in air
On the morning of the second show, dozens of balloons lifted off for a race to Albuquerque
By this song, Phil's bass was booming off the metal grandstand roof
Stretched extra long because Bobby's mic broke; Jerry grew frustrated but then found the riff
Reviewer votes this the best version ever played
Soundboard is excellent and a nice upgrade over the widely circulated high-quality audience recording
Considered one of the year's best shows, with a second set hard to top
Soundboard fills its cuts with audience splices and is far better than an older cassette soundboard the reviewer had
Reviewer ranks it among the best versions ever played, with an extremely electric feel
Help on the Way, Slipknot and Franklin's Tower sequence rated among the best versions ever played
Mix is bass heavy, with the bass washed out or oversaturated, like a decent multigeneration cassette soundboard
Complete soundboard in circulation is repaired with audience splices during a few dropouts; Jonathan Aizen is credited for its arrival
Reviewer calls it among the best versions heard, very electric
Help on the Way into Slipknot! and Franklin's Tower is among the best versions the reviewer has heard
Not a top show of 1983; Sept. 2, 1983 is far better, and the second set beats an uninspired first
Soundboard sound drops in and out frequently, making the quality poor
A spinning circle of over 300 people began mid-song, energizing the band into setbreak and a strong second set
Very good for 1983 but not among the year's best
Pretty good version, but reviewer says many others, such as 5/17/74 and 9/29/77, are better
Matrix of Dankseed's soundboard with an audience DAT from Keith Litzenberger, transferred by Mike Watson
Front-of-board Nakamichi 300 audience tape from Keith Litzenberger's DAT collection, transferred by Mike Watson; taper sat between Tony Suraci's position and this one
During set two tuning, a fan can be heard requesting The Wheel
Crisp and clean, with no cuts at cassette flips, suggesting it was mastered on PCM
Soundboard matrix uses audience source only for the first 2:53 of Alabama Getaway
Clicks and static were cleaned up throughout; some sound-system static remains in an otherwise great-sounding soundboard
Master cassette by Robert Bryant, transferred by Charlie Miller, with Bob Wagner's Nakamichi 700 source supplying patches
A 16-second patch from the Nakamichi 700 source covers the noodle leading into Truckin'
